column1: esteem§The esteem in which she was held by her students never quite reached the committee that decided her tenure.§学生们对她的**敬重**，始终没有传到决定她终身教职的那个委员会那里。§es-（出）+ teem ← estim（估价，同 estimate 估计）→ 看得起
estrangement§The estrangement lasted nine years and ended over a phone call that neither of them had planned to make.§这场**疏远**持续了九年，终结于一通两人都没打算打的电话。§é-（离开）+ strange（陌生）
ethical§The decision was legal and not ethical, and the distinction is what the whole inquiry turned on.§这个决定合法而不**合乎道德**，整场调查正是围绕这一区别展开。§
eulogize§Colleagues eulogized a man they had spent the previous decade quietly working to remove.§同事们**颂扬**一位他们过去十年一直在悄悄设法排挤的人。§eu（好，同 euphoria 欣快）+ log（说，同 dialogue 对话）
eulogy§The eulogy was four minutes long and mentioned no achievement, only the way he listened to people.§这篇**悼词**只有四分钟，没提任何成就，只讲了他听人说话的方式。§
euphemism§"Restructuring" is a euphemism that has cost four hundred people their jobs in this building alone.§「重组」是个**委婉说法**，单在这栋楼里就让四百人失了业。§eu（好）+ phem（说，同 blaspheme 亵渎）→ 说得好听
euphonious§The name was chosen because it was euphonious, not because it described anything the company actually did.§这个名字被选中是因为**悦耳**，而不是因为它描述了公司实际做的任何事。§eu（好）+ phon（声音，同 telephone 电话）
euphoric§The euphoric mood in the office lasted until someone read the contract's termination clause aloud.§办公室里**欣快**的气氛一直持续到有人朗读了合同的终止条款。§eu（好）+ phor（承载，同 metaphor 隐喻）
evade§He evaded the question four times, and the fifth time the interviewer simply read it back word for word.§他**回避**了这个问题四次，第五次采访者只是把它一字不差地又念了一遍。§e-（出）+ vad（走，同 invade 入侵）→ 溜出去
evaluation§The evaluation ran for two years and reached a conclusion the pilot study had reached in four months.§这项**评估**历时两年，得出的结论试点研究四个月就得出了。§e-（出）+ valu（价值，同 value 价值）
evanescent§The colour is evanescent: the dye is brilliant for a season and gone within two years of daylight.§这种颜色**转瞬即逝**——染料鲜艳一季，在日光下两年内消失。§e-（出）+ vanesc（消失，同 vanish 消失）
evenhanded§The most evenhanded account of the dispute was written by someone who had lost money to both sides.§关于这场纠纷最**不偏不倚**的记述，出自一个在双方都赔过钱的人之手。§even（平）+ handed（手）
eventuality§No eventuality in the plan covered the possibility that both suppliers would fail in the same month.§计划中没有任何**可能情况**涵盖两家供应商同月倒闭的情形。§
everlasting§The everlasting argument about the boundary has occupied four generations and moved the fence nine inches.§关于地界的**没完没了**之争占据了四代人，把围栏挪了九英寸。§
evolve§The rule evolved from a memo nobody signed into a requirement nobody can now trace to any authority.§这条规则从一份没人签署的备忘录**演变**成一项如今追不到任何权威依据的要求。§e-（出）+ volv（卷，同 revolve 旋转）→ 一层层展开
exacerbate§The apology exacerbated the situation by explaining, at length, why nothing had actually gone wrong.§这份道歉**加剧**了局面，因为它长篇大论地解释了为什么其实什么问题都没有。§ex-（加强）+ acerb（酸涩，同 acerbic 尖刻的）
exaggerate§He exaggerates by habit rather than design, and the people who work with him mentally halve every number.§他**夸大**是出于习惯而非设计，与他共事的人会自动把每个数字减半。§ex-（出）+ agger（堆积）→ 越堆越高
exaggeration§The exaggeration was tiny and consequential: "most" instead of "many" changed the paper's entire claim.§这处**夸大**微小而后果重大——把「许多」写成「多数」改变了整篇论文的主张。§
exalt§The obituary exalts a career that his own diaries describe as forty years of near-continuous doubt.§这篇讣告**颂扬**了一段职业生涯，而他自己的日记把它描述为四十年几乎不间断的怀疑。§ex-（出）+ alt（高，同 altitude 高度）
exasperation§Her exasperation finally showed in a single sentence, and that sentence is the only part anyone quotes.§她的**恼怒**最终在一句话里露了出来，而那句话是唯一被人引用的部分。§ex-（加强）+ asper（粗糙，同 asperity 严酷）
excavate§They excavated for four seasons and found, in the last week, the wall that justified the entire project.§他们**发掘**了四季，在最后一周找到了那面证明整个项目值得的墙。§ex-（出）+ cav（洞，同 cave 洞穴）
excessive§The force used was excessive by any standard the department itself had published in the previous decade.§按该部门自己过去十年发布的任何标准，动用的武力都是**过度的**。§ex-（出）+ ced（走，同 exceed 超过）
excise§The censor excised nine pages, and the gap is visible in every copy printed before 1989.§审查者**删去**了九页，1989 年前印的每一本都看得出这个缺口。§ex-（出）+ cis（切，同 scissors 剪刀）
excitement§The excitement lasted about a week, and the hard part of the work started the day after it ended.§这份**兴奋**持续约一周，而工作中难的部分在它结束的第二天才开始。§ex-（出）+ cit（唤，同 cite 引用）
exclude§The formula excludes anyone who moved house in the survey year, which is about a fifth of the population.§这个公式**排除**了调查年份内搬过家的所有人，约占人口的五分之一。§ex-（出）+ clud（关闭，同 include 包括）
exclusive§The interview was exclusive for about ninety minutes, after which four other outlets ran the same quotes.§这次采访**独家**了约九十分钟，此后四家媒体登出了同样的引语。§
excursion§What was billed as a scientific excursion turned into nine days of rain and one very good photograph.§一次号称科学**考察**的出行变成了九天的雨和一张非常好的照片。§ex-（出）+ curs（跑，同 current 水流）→ 跑出去一趟
execution§The idea was sound and the execution was not, which is the diagnosis in roughly nine failures out of ten.§想法站得住而**执行**不行，这是十次失败里约九次的诊断。§ex-（出）+ sequ（跟随，同 sequence 序列）→ 一步步做到底
exemplary§Her record was exemplary until a single lapse that the board treated as if it were the whole record.§她的履历一直**堪称典范**，直到一次失误被董事会当成了全部履历。§exempl（样本，同 example 例子）
exempt§Small workshops are exempt from the rule, and about seventy percent of the industry is a small workshop.§小作坊**豁免**于这条规则，而该行业约七成是小作坊。§ex-（出）+ empt（拿，同 exempt 取出）→ 拿出去不算
exhaustive§The search was exhaustive rather than clever: they read every one of the four thousand files by hand.§这次检索是**穷尽式的**而非取巧的——他们把四千份卷宗逐一手工读完。§ex-（出）+ haust（汲取）→ 抽干为止
exhibit§The museum exhibits the letter beside a forgery of it, and most visitors pick the wrong one.§博物馆把这封信与它的一份赝品并列**展出**，多数参观者选错了。§ex-（出）+ hibit（拿住，同 prohibit 禁止）
exhilarate§The first descent exhilarated her so completely that she signed up for the whole season that evening.§第一次下坡**让她兴奋**得那么彻底，当晚就报了整个赛季。§ex-（加强）+ hilar（快活，同 hilarious 滑稽的）
exorbitant§The fee is exorbitant only because there is no alternative: the same service costs a tenth abroad.§这笔费用**高得离谱**仅仅因为别无选择——同样的服务在国外只要十分之一。§ex-（出）+ orbit（轨道）→ 出了正常轨道
exotic§The plant was exotic in 1840 and is now the commonest weed on every railway embankment in the country.§这种植物在 1840 年还是**外来的**稀罕物，如今是全国每条铁路路基上最常见的野草。§exo（外面）
expansion§The expansion doubled capacity and tripled the debt, and only one of those two numbers appeared in the announcement.§这次**扩张**使产能翻倍、债务翻三倍，而公告里只出现了其中一个数字。§ex-（出）+ pand（展开，同 expand 扩张）
expansive§He was expansive after dinner and gave away, in twenty minutes, what four months of negotiation had protected.§他晚饭后变得**健谈豪爽**，二十分钟里说漏了四个月谈判所保护的东西。§
expediency§The decision was made on grounds of expediency and defended, afterward, on grounds of principle.§这个决定是出于**权宜**做出的，事后却以原则为由辩护。§ex-（出）+ ped（脚，同 pedal 踏板）→ 先把脚从泥里拔出来
expedient§Cutting the training budget was expedient in March and, by the September audit, plainly catastrophic for the whole line.§砍掉培训预算在三月是**权宜之计**，到九月审计时对整条生产线已明显是场灾难。§
expedite§A single phone call from the mayor expedited a permit that had sat unexamined for fourteen months.§市长的一通电话**加快**了一份搁置十四个月无人审查的许可。§ex-（出）+ ped（脚）→ 解开脚镣让它快走
expeditious§The response was expeditious for once: the crew arrived in nineteen minutes and had power back by noon.§这次的响应难得**迅速**——抢修队十九分钟就到，中午前恢复了供电。§
expendable§Treating the night shift as expendable worked until the night shift was the only crew who knew the machine.§把夜班当成**可牺牲的**一直行得通，直到夜班成了唯一懂这台机器的人。§ex-（出）+ pend（花费，同 spend 花费）
experimental§The treatment is still experimental, and the waiting list for the trial runs to four thousand names.§这种疗法仍处于**实验阶段**，试验的等候名单上有四千个名字。§
experimentation§Years of patient experimentation produced one useful compound and nine hundred that did nothing at all.§多年耐心的**实验**产出一种有用的化合物，另外九百种毫无作用。§
expertise§The expertise sat two floors below the decision, and nobody thought to walk downstairs and ask.§**专业知识**就在决策层下面两层楼，却没人想到下楼去问一句。§expert（内行）
explanatory§The explanatory note is longer than the rule it explains and considerably harder to understand.§这条**解释性**说明比它所解释的规则还长，也难懂得多。§
explosive§Growth in the sector was explosive for three years and then stopped so abruptly that nobody had a plan.§该行业的增长**爆炸性地**持续了三年，随后戛然而止，谁也没有预案。§ex-（出）+ plod（拍手驱赶，同 applaud 鼓掌）

expropriate§The state expropriated four hundred hectares and paid compensation calculated on prices from eleven years earlier.§国家**征用**了四百公顷土地，补偿却按十一年前的价格计算。§ex-（出）+ propri（自己的，同 property 财产）→ 从私人手里拿走
expropriation§The expropriation was legal, sudden, and complete, and the families learned about it from a notice on a fence.§这次**征收**合法、突然而彻底，那些家庭是从围栏上的一张告示得知的。§
expurgate§Editors expurgated the diaries before publication, and the deleted passages surfaced in an auction sixty years later.§编者在出版前**删净**了这些日记，被删段落六十年后在一场拍卖中现身。§ex-（出）+ purg（清洁，同 purge 清洗）
extant§Only four copies are extant, and one of them has been in the same family since 1743.§现**存**仅四本，其中一本自 1743 年起一直在同一个家族手中。§ex-（出）+ st（站立，同 stand 站）→ 还立着的

extemporaneous§His extemporaneous reply was better than the prepared speech, and the transcript shows exactly where he abandoned the text.§他**即席的**回答胜过准备好的讲稿，文字记录清楚显示他从哪里开始脱稿。§ex-（出）+ tempor（时间，同 temporary 临时的）→ 当场就来
extend§The deadline was extended twice for reasons that had nothing to do with the work and everything to do with the calendar.§期限被**延长**了两次，理由与工作全然无关，与日程则大有关系。§ex-（出）+ tend（伸展，同 tension 张力）
extensive§The damage was extensive but shallow: nine hundred items affected, none of them beyond repair.§损坏**范围广**却不深——九百件物品受影响，无一无法修复。§
extenuate§Nothing in the file extenuates the delay, though the letter from the department spends four pages trying.§卷宗里没有任何内容能**减轻**这次延误的责任，尽管部门的信用四页试图这么做。§ex-（出）+ tenu（薄，同 tenuous 纤细的）→ 把罪责说薄
external§The external review found what four internal reviews had missed, which surprised nobody outside the organization.§这次**外部**评审发现了四次内部评审漏掉的问题，这没让组织外的任何人意外。§
extinct§The bird was declared extinct in 1962 and then photographed, almost certainly, by a farmer in 2004.§这种鸟于 1962 年被宣布**灭绝**，随后在 2004 年几乎可以确定被一位农民拍到过。§ex-（出）+ stinct（刺／熄，同 distinguish 区分）→ 火被彻底掐灭
extinction§Extinction rarely has one cause: this species lost its forest, its river, and its main food within forty years.§**灭绝**很少只有一个原因——这个物种在四十年内失去了森林、河流和主要食物。§
extol§Reviewers extolled the design and said nothing about the fact that it costs four times as much to maintain.§评论者**盛赞**这个设计，对它的维护费高出四倍只字未提。§ex-（出）+ tol（举起，同 tolerate 容忍）→ 高高举起
extract§Researchers extracted usable DNA from a tooth that had been in a museum drawer since 1911.§研究者从一颗自 1911 年起就躺在博物馆抽屉里的牙齿中**提取**出可用的 DNA。§ex-（出）+ tract（拉，同 attract 吸引）
extraneous§Nine of the eleven appendices are extraneous, and removing them would make the argument considerably clearer.§十一个附录里有九个是**多余的**，删掉它们会让论证清楚得多。§extra（外面）→ 外来的、不相干的
extravagance§The extravagance of the opening night was remembered long after everyone had forgotten the production itself.§首演之夜的**奢华**在人们忘记演出本身之后很久仍被记着。§extra（超出）+ vag（游荡，同 vague 模糊的）→ 走过头
extravagant§His extravagant claims for the device were repeated by four newspapers and tested by none of them.§他对这台装置**夸张的**宣称被四家报纸转载，无一家做过测试。§
extremist§The extremist position won the vote because the moderates split three ways and never met to decide otherwise.§**极端**立场赢得投票，是因为温和派分成三派，也从未碰头商量别的办法。§extrem（最外，同 extreme 极端）
